hints: The answer is a boundary: every position before it holds a reading below the target, every position from it on holds one that is not.
Binary search for that boundary rather than for the target itself. The question at each step is `readings[mid] < target`, which is always answerable.
Keep a half-open range `[low, high)` starting as `[0, n)`. When `readings[mid] < target`, the answer is above `mid`, so `low = mid + 1`; otherwise `high = mid`.
The loop ends when `low == high`, and that value is the answer - including `n`, which is why `high` starts at `n` and not `n - 1`.
